issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a function named simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) but the template repository defines a function named simulate_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) instead. Additionally, the template's plot_msd calls simulate_msd_one_round, which doesn't exist in the template. This name/signature mismatch will confuse students and cause runtime/import errors or failing tests expecting simulate_msd_one_round.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template and problem statement consistent: rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (keeping the same parameters and behavior), or update plot_msd and the problem statement to call/require simulate_one_round. Ensure the function name used in tests, plot_msd, and the problem description all match.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the simulation function as simulate_msd_one_round, but the template defines it as simulate_one_round (and even raises a NotImplementedError mentioning simulate_msd_one_round). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entry point (run one-round MSD simulation) will confuse students: tests and other parts of the template (e.g., plot_msd) call simulate_msd_one_round, which does not exist in the template, while the template's stub uses a different name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the name across artifacts. Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (update its def, docstring, and the NotImplementedError message), or alternatively change the problem statement and solution usages to simulate_one_round. Prefer keeping simulate_msd_one_round to match the problem wording and solution implementation.
